You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task notes

## task-87697ebd: continue diagonal ray(s)
Verified solved test (2026-10-21): Given sparse colored diagonal seeds on a zero background, extend the indicated diagonal line(s) in the same direction(s) to the grid edge, retaining all original cells and colors. Test 10x8 input had [6,6] on row 1 cols 2-3, plus a 4 at r2c3 and r3c4; output kept input and extended color 4 diagonally down-right at r4c5, r5c6, r6c7, r7c8, stopping at grid boundary. Correct with 0 wrong submissions after requesting two demos. Demo 1 (background 4) showed color-1 diagonal from r4c3/r3c4 extending down-left to r5c2; existing other cells unchanged. Demo 2 had separate rays: color 9 extends down-left one cell per row from r3c2 and color 8 extends down-right from r3c15; both continue through boundary, while initial unrelated seeds (5,6,9,8) retained. Infer direction from aligned diagonal seed(s); extend only the corresponding ray(s), preserving original pattern and background. Do not fill intervening cells or extend the other isolated motif colors unless they form a line.

## task-dbb85d02: horizontal paired bars
Observed task family: mostly uniform background with separated horizontal motifs. In simple cases, preserve bars and recolor only contiguous background tail cells to their right with color 1 when target bar ends before the grid edge; full-width bars unchanged. Patterned motifs need context: only select the corresponding bars identified by the repeated motif, not every partial bar. Examples include changes to specific tails in the lower repeated motifs. Generalize cautiously and inspect motif structure.

## task-766879a9: aligned panels and shared-color coincidence mask
Verified solved test (2026-10-21) after two demos. Input consists of two equal-sized noisy panels separated by a uniform divider row or column. Each panel uses two colors, with exactly one color shared between both panels. Output is the cellwise agreement mask for the shared color: dimensions equal one panel; fill output with the shared color, except output 3 wherever the aligned cell in BOTH panels is that shared color. Compare aligned coordinates directly; do not reverse/flip panels; exclude divider.

Evidence from demos: horizontal demo 1 had divider color 4, upper palette {1,5}, lower palette {2,5}; shared color=5, output 9x21 filled with 5 and 3 exactly where both corresponding cells were 5. Vertical demo 2 had divider color 7, left palette {8,5}, right palette {8,1}; shared=8, output 24x7 filled with 8 and 3 where both aligned panel cells were 8. Solved test had divider row of 4s, top palette {6,2}, bottom palette {5,2}; shared=2. Output 10x15 had base 2, with 3 at the positions where corresponding cells in top 10x15 and bottom 10x15 panels both equaled 2. Only the first 10 rows above the divider and rows 11-20 below it are panels; row 10 is divider.

The task is robust to divider orientation and differing panel-specific colors. To solve: identify the separator; split into equal panels; find their common palette color (not divider); output panel size with shared-color base and mark 3 only at intersections where both aligned inputs equal the shared color. Avoid returning the panel itself or merely converting one panel's foreground.

Additional verified test (2026-10-21): 9x23 input with a full-height divider column of 5 at column 12; left 9x11 panel palette {4,6}, right 9x11 panel palette {1,6}, so shared color=6. Output is 9x11 filled with 6, with 3 only at aligned coordinates where both panels have 6. In this test the only such coordinate was row 5, column 5 (1-based). This confirmed the vertical split interpretation and exact coincidence rule.

Additional verified test (2026-10-21): 29x2 input, with divider row [0,0] at row 15. The upper 14x2 panel uses colors {8,1}; lower 14x2 panel (rows 16-29) uses {4,1}; shared color=1. Output is 14x2, base 1, with 3 exactly at aligned positions where both panels contain 1. Correct output (1-based positions marked 3): r2 c2; r3 c2; r5 c2; r8 c1; r10 c1; r12 c2; r13 c2. Exact output: [[1,1],[1,3],[1,3],[1,1],[1,3],[1,1],[1,1],[3,1],[1,1],[3,1],[1,1],[1,3],[1,3],[1,1]]. My first answer was wrong because it marked some individual 1s without verifying the aligned cell in the other panel, and marked both cells in a row where only column 2 matched. Reminder: a cell is 3 only if BOTH aligned panel cells equal the shared color; a shared-color cell in just one panel remains base color.

Additional verified test (2026-10-21): task-766879a9, input 2x19, with zero divider column at c10. The two 2x9 panels are columns 1-9 and 11-19. Left palette {6,7}, right palette {4,6}, shared color=6. Output is 2x9 filled with 6; mark 3 only when both corresponding cells are 6. Only matching coordinate was output row 2, column 4, so output [[6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6],[6,6,6,3,6,6,6,6,6]]. This validates the shared-color coincidence rule for a very narrow horizontal split with a single-column divider.

Additional verified test (2026-10-21): task-766879a9, input 29x2, with row 15 [8,8] as the divider. The top 14x2 panel uses {9,7}, and bottom 14x2 panel (rows 16-29) uses {7,5}; shared color=7. Output is 14x2, base 7, with 3 exactly where aligned cells in both panels are 7. Correct output: [[7,3],[3,7],[3,7],[7,3],[3,7],[7,3],[7,3],[3,3],[3,7],[3,3],[7,3],[7,3],[3,7],[7,7]]. A first attempt incorrectly marked the final output cell (row 14, col 2) as 3; the aligned upper cell is 9, so it must remain 7. This reinforces: only mark 3 where both aligned panel cells equal the shared color, including at the panel edge.

Additional verified test (2026-10-21): task-766879a9, input 15x14 with a horizontal divider row of 9s at row 8. The top 7x14 panel uses {8,1}; the bottom 7x14 panel (rows 9-15) uses {7,1}; shared color=1. Compare aligned coordinates directly, indexing each panel from its own first row. None of the 1-cells coincide at the same panel-relative row and column, so the correct output is a 7x14 grid filled entirely with 1 (no 3s). My first submission incorrectly marked output row 4, column 2 due to a misalignment/visual comparison; after correcting the aligned-coordinate check, the all-1 output was accepted. Lesson: do not infer a match from nearby/repeated 1s—verify the same column in the corresponding row of both panels. The task can have zero coincidence cells.

Additional verified test (2026-10-21): task-766879a9, 17x29 input, vertical divider column 15 (value 0), panels are 17x14 at cols 1-14 and 16-29. Left palette {9,2}, right palette {5,9}, shared color=9. Output is 17x14 with base 9 and 3 only where left panel cell and corresponding right-panel cell are both 9. Accepted output:
[[9,9,3,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9],[9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,3,9,9,9],[9,9,3,9,9,9,9,9,9,3,9,9,9,9],[3,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9],[9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9],[9,9,9,9,9,3,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9],[9,9,9,3,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9],[9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9],[9,3,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,3],[9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,3,9,9,9],[9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9],[9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9],[9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9],[3,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9],[9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9],[9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9],[9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9,9]].
Important failure lesson: do not infer output marks merely from right-panel deviations or approximately aligned visual patterns; mark 3 only at exact same panel-relative coordinate where both values are 9. Earlier wrong attempts repeatedly misindexed row 2 (mark is c11, not c10), row 3 (marks c3 and c10), and row 10 (mark c11). To avoid drift, use 1-based indexing and validate each candidate against both panels before submitting; right-panel 9 candidates for this input are: r1c3, r2c11, r3c3/c10, r4c1, r6c6, r7c4, r9c2/c14, r10c11, r14c1. These are the complete set of output 3 coordinates (all other output cells remain 9).

Additional verified test (2026-10-21): task-766879a9, 12x15 input with vertical divider column 8 (value 8); left and right panels each 12x7. Left palette {1,2}, right palette {4,1}; shared color=1. Output 12x7 has base 1, marking 3 only at exact aligned coordinates where both panels contain 1. Accepted output marks were r1c4, r6c6, r11c3, and r11c5 (1-based); every other cell is 1. Right-panel 1 candidates at r1c4, r4c3, r6c6, r11c3/c5; r4c3 is NOT a match because left panel has 2 at that coordinate. This again confirms matching is literal same-coordinate coincidence, not merely selecting all shared-color occurrences from either panel.

## task-56789af0: complete periodic color pattern
Additional verified test (2026-10-21): 9x9 grid with full-width row clues r1=5, r3=2, r4=1, r5-r7=9, r9=9; r2 and r8 are zero rows. Accepted output fills rows with the period-7 sequence [5,9,2,1,9,9,9], repeated by row index: output row colors [5,9,2,1,9,9,9,5,9]. This establishes that period can be longer than the number of distinct colors and can include repeated 9s; align known rows by row index (e.g. r1 and r8 same phase, r2 and r9 same phase) and fill zeros with that phase's color.
Verified solved test (2026-10-21). Grid is a sparse encoding of a repeating color pattern: retain the full-width colored row anchors and fill zero rows with the inferred repeating sequence/phase. In the solved 25x25 test, anchors were row 5=3, row 7=7, row 18=9, row 24=1. The inferred 4-row cycle, starting at row 1, was [3,9,7,1], repeated through all 25 rows; accepted output has row colors 3,9,7,1 repeating (thus every fifth row is 3). Derivation: row5=3, row7=7, row18=9, row24=1 all agree with that cycle. Demo 1 (13x13) also showed retaining repeated adjacent same-color anchors: input had anchors r2=2,r3=1,r5=8,r7-8=9,r11=4,r13=5; output row sequence was [9,2,1,4,8,5,9,9,2,1,4,8,5]. Another demo (16x16) encoded a two-dimensional periodic color motif with diagonal sparse tracks; output expanded/tiled a periodic pattern. Generalize by locating periodicity and phase from anchors, and preserve explicit repeated-color positions rather than forcing a simplistic period where anchors contradict it.

Additional verified test (2026-10-21): task-56789af0, test input [[9,3],[0,9]] was accepted as [[9,3],[3,9]]. The zero is the missing cell in a two-color diagonal periodic motif and is filled with 3, yielding alternating 9/3 across rows and columns. Demo 1 showed a 24x24 sparse diagonal-track encoding using colors 7 and 4 expanded into a 3x3-periodic pattern tiled across the grid; row patterns cycle with period 3. Demo 2 was an already-complete 6x6 grid of full-width color rows and was returned unchanged. Use the visible sparse motif/period and phase; do not assume all instances require expansion or one universal period.

Additional verified test (2026-10-21): task-56789af0, 20x20 input with sparse down-left anti-diagonal tracks was solved and accepted using a period-3 coloring by 1-based r+c residue. Input clues: color 7 on sum r+c=4 and 30 (residues 1 and 0 mod 3), color 9 on sum 35 (residue 2 mod 3). Correct output: 7 wherever (r+c) mod 3 is 0 or 1, and 9 wherever it is 2. Equivalently repeating row patterns start row1 [9,7,7] and cycle shifts each row: row2 [7,7,9], row3 [7,9,7], then repeat. This exact rule was accepted after three wrong submissions. Failed hypotheses: simple checkerboard (sum parity) was wrong, and mod-13 sparse-line filling was wrong. Lesson: use all same-orientation diagonal tracks to infer the smallest residue period and map each residue; multiple residues can share a color (here two classes -> 7, one -> 9).

Additional verified test (2026-10-21): task-56789af0, 30x30 input with full-width row clues at r1=9, r2=7, r9=2, r28=2, r30=8 and all other rows zero. Accepted output is the 5-row sequence [9,7,2,2,8] repeated down all 30 rows. This was solved with no wrong submissions after requesting two demos. Demo 1 (21x21) confirms sparse full-width row clues represent a repeating vertical sequence: output row colors cycle [3,2,9,8,5] from row 1; observed clues r3=9, r4=8, r12=2, r15=5, r21=3. Demo 2 (6x6) has only r1=5 and r6=6, and expands to alternating rows [5,6,5,6,5,6], so period may be as short as 2. For these horizontal full-row clue cases, identify row-index period and phase by aligning all nonzero clue rows, then fill each entire zero row with its sequence color; keep clue rows as given. The current test pattern has two consecutive 2 rows within each 5-row cycle.

Additional verified test (2026-10-21): task-56789af0, 17x17 sparse full-width horizontal row clues; accepted output consists of row colors [8,4,5,1,4,5] repeated with period 6. Clues: r2=4, r4=1, r5=4, r7=8, r9=5, r12=5; these fix the sequence phase and validate the period. Fill each zero row with the corresponding color in this cycle and retain clue rows. The accepted 17-row sequence was [8,4,5,1,4,5,8,4,5,1,4,5,8,4,5,1,4].

## task-87697ebd: continue diagonal ray(s) — additional verified case (2026-10-21)
26x11 test with background 4: the 7 pair at r5c8 and r6c9 establishes a down-right diagonal; extend it backward up-left from r5c8 to r4c7, r3c6, r2c5, r1c4, preserving seeds. The 6 pair at r7c9 and r8c8 establishes a down-left diagonal; continue from r9c7 through r15c1 to the edge. Leave other colors unchanged when they do not form an indicated diagonal ray; here the 8s at r6c10, r7c10, r8c11 do not constitute a diagonal pair in one direction and were retained as-is. Accepted output used exactly these added cells (and no other changes). Important lesson from the wrong first submission: extending the 6 ray alone is incomplete; also extend the 7 ray in its established diagonal direction, including backward toward the boundary. The task rule remains: infer each ray direction from aligned seeds, extend along that same diagonal to the grid edge, retain all original cells/colors, and do not add unindicated diagonals. Supporting demo 1 (23x14) had 9s at r13c1-c2 and r14c3; output extended the down-right 9 ray from r14c3 to r23c12, while retaining other original cells (including 8 at r12c1 and 5 at r12c2). Supporting demo 2 showed no extension when apparent nearby colored cells did not form a valid pair/ray: 10x10 grid with 0s at r7c10,r8c9 and r8c10 plus 8 at r9c8 and 7 at r9c9 was unchanged. This suggests the line needs clear same-color diagonal alignment; isolated or adjacent competing cells don't automatically imply extension.

A color-2 diagonal pair at r7c4 and r8c5 (1-based) indicated the down-right ray; extend it backward up-left from r7c4 through r6c3, r5c2, r4c1 to the boundary. Preserve original cells, including unrelated 3 at r8c6 and 6 at r9c6; do not extend them. Accepted output matched this exact extension with 0 wrong attempts.
